subject: SableWorks — post-call: inference deep-dive, SLOs & next technical asks
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rana <aisha.rana@sableworks.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@sableworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: SableWorks — post-call: inference deep-dive, SLOs & next technical asks

Thanks again for the call today — really useful context. Quick recap of what we took away and the specific asks so we can align our engineering follow-up. Please correct me where I’m off.

High-level pain points you emphasized:
- Peak throughput: ingesting ~600 reqs/s for short summarization jobs (avg 160 tokens output).
- Tight P95 latency requirement for interactive use: target 250–350ms per request (user-experienced end-to-end).
- Model quality: must maintain current fine-tuned summarization quality (custom prompt + 8k context) — accuracy regressions >2% are unacceptable.
- Data controls: all PII must stay in your VPC for the pilot; logs need to be auditable for SOC2 review.

Primary goals agreed:
1) Proof-of-concept: meet 250ms p95 for 90% of interactive traffic with our hosted dedicated pool (pilot environment).
2) Cost target: keep inference unit cost close to your current on-prem baseline — aim to reduce or match by 10% in production.
3) Rollout path: start with dedicated capacity in us-west, evaluate private deployment if compliance checks require air-gapped.

Specific technical asks from your team (from Tom/Aisha):
- Baseline concurrency/throughput targets per model variant (we listed 600 reqs/s peak).
- Required context window: 8k tokens for end-to-end summarization use cases; occasional 16k for long documents.
- Acceptable quantization: you can tolerate FP16 but not heavy 4-bit quant for the initial pilot because of quality concerns.
- Warm cache expectations: cold-starts must be bounded (p95 cold-start < 1.2s).
- KV cache reuse pattern: typical conversation prefix reuse ~30% across requests.

Proposed Redwood approach (short):
- Dedicated pool (GPU subset) with model variants pinned per stage (gpt-style 7B/13B fine-tuned variants).
- Smart routing to lower-cost variant for batch background jobs; canary traffic stays on higher-fidelity variant.
- KV/prefix caching + request coalescing to hit throughput while keeping tail latency low.
- Isolation & audit: pilot runs in a dedicated VPC with KMS integration for keys; retention policy can be configured per-tenant.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll send a short spreadsheet capturing the throughput/latency matrix for your expected traffic shapes (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-min deep-dive with our runtime engineer (Marissa) next week to validate kernel/quantization choices and a topology sketch.
3) We’ll share a runbook template for the pilot that includes rollback/fallback and KPIs we’ll measure.

If that aligns, can you confirm the best times next Wed/Thu for the deep-dive? Also flag any other must-haves we missed (esp. around e2e logging or retention windows).

Thanks,
Connor O’Brien
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 20271114-sableworks-call-notes.pdf (application/pdf, 24KB)]
From: Aisha Rana <aisha.rana@sableworks.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@sableworks.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SableWorks — post-call: inference deep-dive, SLOs & next technical asks

Connor — thanks for the crisp recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications before the deep-dive so we can prep numbers on our side:

1) Throughput shape: 600 reqs/s is our peak for the web editor during marketing hours; base load is ~120 reqs/s. Spikes can be bursty for 30–90s.
2) P95 latency target 250–350ms is strict for the editor; background bulk summarization can be relaxed to 1s p95.
3) Context: 8k is the default; ~5% of jobs hit 16k and we’d like a fallback that gracefully degrades to multi-pass summarization if 16k isn't available.
4) Privacy: for the pilot we need logs redacted and stored for 90 days; we will provide a SOC2 packet during procurement.

Questions for your engineering team before the call:
- Do you have a recommended model family (smaller quantized variant vs larger full-precision) given our 8k/16k needs?
- How does Redwood enforce p95 cold-start limits when autoscaling is in play?
- Any constraints on batching that would risk pushing p95 above our target for interactive requests?

I’ve attached a simple CSV with our traffic histogram to help sizing. Will also share our SOC2 contact after internal confirmation.

Best,
Aisha Rana
Head of Product — SableWorks
[Attachment: sable_requests_table.csv (text/csv, 4KB)]

On Mon, Nov 15, 2027 at 08:00, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@sableworks.com> wrote:
> Add: for the pilot we want a hard SLA-like escalation path if latency breaches >3 consecutive p95 windows.
> —Tom
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SableWorks — post-call: inference deep-dive, SLOs & next technical asks

Marissa/Markus — forwarding SableWorks' clarifying notes and their traffic histogram. Key asks for the engineering deep-dive:

- Peak 600 reqs/s, base ~120 reqs/s; spikes 30–90s. Burst tolerance required.
- Interactive p95 250–350ms (target); background jobs 1s p95.
- 8k default context, occasional 16k. Avoid heavy 4-bit for pilot.
- Cold-start p95 target <1.2s.
- Audit/log redaction + 90d retention. They may require SOC2 packet.
- Escalation: they want automated alerting and an escalation path if p95 breaches for 3 consecutive windows.

Initial thoughts / suggested topology for discussion (high level):
1) Dedicated GPU pool in us-west (2x node pools):
   - Pool A (interactive): lower-latency config, pinned model variant (FP16 13B) with local KV cache and aggressive prefix caching.
   - Pool B (batch): cost-optimized (INT8/quant) for nightly bulk summarization; auto-route non-interactive jobs here.
2) Fronting layer: request classifier that tags interactive vs background, enforces routing and priority queues.
3) Autoscaling: proactive warm pools + pre-warming policy based on their histogram to limit cold-starts; set minimum replica floor for Pool A to meet p95.
4) Fallbacks: when 16k requested, either on-the-fly multistep summarization (2-pass) or fall back to a higher-memory variant (if available).
5) Observability: per-request tracing to capture token-level latency, and a p95 alerting rule that triggers Redwood on-call + a SableWorks escalation webhook.

Can you validate feasibility and note any kernel/quantization caveats (esp. 8k vs 16k memory impacts), and identify what info we must collect from SableWorks ahead of the call (e.g., sample payload sizes, acceptance test prompts)?

I scheduled the deep-dive as a tentative: Wed 2027-11-17 09:30 PT — please confirm availability or suggest alternatives.

Thanks,
Connor
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rana <aisha.rana@sableworks.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@sableworks.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SableWorks — post-call: inference deep-dive, SLOs & next technical asks

Connor / team / Aisha — confirmed, this is feasible for an initial pilot. Quick engineering readout ahead of the deep-dive:

- Model family: recommend FP16 13B fine-tuned baseline for interactive (best quality/latency balance). For bulk batch jobs we can use an INT8 7B variant; we’ll quantify expected quality delta on your sample prompts.
- 8k/16k: 8k is well-supported. 16k will increase KV size approx 2x–2.5x memory and requires either larger instance types or a multi-chunk strategy; we’ll prepare cost/latency estimates for both.
- Cold-starts: we will configure a warm-min pool with proactive pre-warm based on histogram. P95 cold-start <1.2s is realistic with warm-min and pre-warm hooks; we’ll validate during load testing.
- Batching constraints: interactive queue will cap batch sizes to preserve latency (we’ll enforce batch caps + dynamic batching window). Background queue can batch aggressively.
- Observability & escalation: we’ll provide a dashboard link and configure a p95 rolling alert with a 3-window suppression policy + webhook to your PagerDuty.

Pre-call ask from engineering: please send a small set (10) of representative prompts and a sample of payload size distribution so we can run quick local profiling on our kernels. Also confirm whether any prompts include long metadata fields that inflate token counts.

I’ll bring a topology sketch to the Wed deep-dive and run through kernel/instance choices. Connor — the tentative time works for me; Markus, can you join too?

-Marissa
Engineering Manager — Redwood Inference
